ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As illustrated in the diagram, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle BAC=90^\circ$ and $\angle B=45^\circ$. A line is drawn from point A such that $AD \parallel BC$, with point D being to the right of point A. Points P and Q are respectively on rays $AD$ and $CB$. Point E is a point on segment $CQ$ and $CQ=2AP$. Let $AP=x$ and $CE=y$, it follows that $y=2x-2$. When point Q is the midpoint of $BC$, $y=3$. What are the lengths of $QE$ and $BC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}:
As shown in the figure below,\\
Given that $y=3$, that is $3=2x-2$,\\
we find $x=\frac{5}{2}$, thus $AP=\frac{5}{2}$,\\
$\therefore CE=y=2x-2=2\times \frac{5}{2}-2=3$, $CQ=2AP=2\times \frac{5}{2}=5$,\\
$\therefore QE=CQ-CE=5-3=\boxed{2}$,\\
$\because$ point Q is the midpoint of BC,\\
$\therefore BC=2CQ=2\times 5=\boxed{10}$;
